title: Rufus Darpoh, a dedicated journalist in Liberia, has faced significant challenges in his career due to his commitment to unbiased reporting. He began his career during the Tolbert era and continued through the military takeover in 1980. Darpoh served as editor-in-chief of the state-owned New Liberian but was dismissed in 1983 for publishing opinions contrary to government policy. After his dismissal, he worked in various roles while maintaining his journalistic pursuits. Recently, he was arrested by the National Security Agency for allegedly transmitting news against the government's interests, and he is currently detained under harsh conditions without formal charges. An appeal for his release is encouraged, emphasizing human rights concerns without political bias.
